title: Variant anchoring orchestration and perf-manifest publisher for hetero GPU SKUs
creator: Asha Khatri
description: Introduce an orchestration component that creates and publishes hardware-specific performance manifests (A100/H100/L40S/MI300 variants) and anchors model versions to stable variant identifiers. The goal is to ensure deterministic routing, automatic fallback compatibility, and reproducible latency/cost expectations for newly onboarded model versions across heterogeneous GPU SKUs.
acceptance_criteria: Perf-manifest generator produces JSON manifests for A100/H100/L40S/MI300 with fields: latency_p50, latency_p95, tokens_per_sec, kv_footprint_bytes, warm_cold_delta, recommended_quant_profile
Published manifests land in S3 with semantic versioning and a manifest index used by the router
Variant anchoring API accepts model_name + model_revision and returns an immutable anchor ID tied to a specific manifest version
Router accepts anchor ID and applies routing policies (latency SLO, cost tier, region) and falls back to compatible anchors when capacity constrained
Automated test harness validates manifest stability across 3 independent runs and flags >5% p95 variance
Documentation and SDK examples added to onboarding guide and Console model page
steps: Design manifest schema with product and runtime stakeholders (include warm/cold metrics and quant recommendations)
Extend telemetry pipeline to emit per-sample perf traces tagged by hardware SKU and model revision
Implement generator job: aggregate traces -> apply outlier rejection -> compute percentiles and KV footprint -> produce manifest
Build publisher: S3+index writer + atomic tag (manifest:vX) + publish webhooks for Console and Router
Create anchor service: map (model,revision) -> anchor_id and store manifest version pointer
Integrate Router: accept anchor_id, check manifest compatibility, implement fallback heuristics
Add e2e tests in CI: synthetic workloads on each SKU using the public perf suite
Console UI: surface manifest diffs, release history, and 'anchor' button for PM/owner approval
decisions: Use manifest-first approach rather than per-device dynamic micro-benchmarking: reduces onboarding wall-time and centralizes stability gating
Anchor IDs will be immutable; manifest versions are referenceable and new manifests require an explicit 'promote' action
Outlier rejection will use median absolute deviation (MAD) with a tunable threshold (default 3x MAD)
Store manifests in S3 with manifest-index TTL of 90 days and a long-term archive for older pinned versions
Fallback heuristic favors lower-cost compatible anchors if latency SLO is not strict, otherwise prefers same-architecture variants
risks: Telemetry sparsity on low-traffic models may produce noisy manifests — mitigation: require a minimum sample count and fallback to historical priors
Mislabelled SKU telemetry leading to incorrect manifests — mitigation: add SKU validation checks and cross-checks with infra inventory
Consumers relying on anchor immutability may be surprised by manifest promotion — mitigation: require explicit approvals and a 24h pre-promote announcement window
Large manifest churn could complicate router caching — mitigation: implement cache-busting TTLs and delta-aware refresh
